title: Turn social media market chatter into paper trade ideas
summary: A trader's automated X scan spotted a volatility signal, and his research agent, Tape, confirmed it before he placed a paper Nasdaq options trade.
agent_role: An automated scan flagged a post about Nasdaq volatility, and a research agent named Tape checked the data. The trade itself was a paper trade decided with the human.
outcome: The author reports a paper trade with an estimated 84% chance of profit and a plan to close at 50% profit; no final result is stated.
what_they_did: A trader runs an automated scan of X posts. It caught a market analyst noting Nasdaq swings running high compared with the S&P 500. His research agent, Tape, confirmed the gap was near its widest in a month. He then placed a practice options trade with no real money.
how_it_went: He says the trade had about an 84% estimated chance of profit, with a plan to close at 50% profit. The post gives no final result.
worth_knowing: This was a paper trade, meaning practice with no real money at stake.
prompt: Each morning before the market opens, scan posts from [list of market accounts] for comments about [market signal, e.g. unusual volatility]. When you find one, check it against recent market data and tell me if it holds up, with numbers and sources. Then suggest one paper trade idea that fits [my risk limits], explain the reasoning and the risks, and log it in [a spreadsheet]. Do not place any real trades. Wait for my review before logging anything as taken.

curation.rationale: A genuine finance workflow where an automated scan and a research agent led to a paper options trade, but it is very brief with no setup details or final result.
